title: Dover vs Ashby: Complete Comparison for Startup Hiring (August 2026)
summary: Compare Dover vs Ashby recruiting software for startups in August 2026. Dover offers free ATS with fractional recruiters while Ashby costs $300+ monthly.
body_markdown:
Looking at Ashby vs Dover comes down to what stage your company is at right now. If you’re a founder or small team filling a handful of roles, you need[recruiting software](https://www.dover.com/) that’s ready to go immediately. Let’s walk through what each tool does differently so you can pick the one that matches where you are today.


**TLDR:**


-


Dover offers a free ATS with job board distribution to 100+ sites; AI resume scoring is available on the $199/month premium plan


-


You pay an average of $2K-7K per hire with Dover’s fractional recruiters vs $30K+ for agencies (rates vary)


-


Ashby costs around $400/month minimum (Foundations plan) and requires days of training to use effectively


-


Dover’s setup takes minutes with no configuration; Ashby needs extensive system optimization


-


Dover combines free recruiting software with on-demand hourly recruiters for startups


## Dover vs Ashby: Quick Comparison


**Dover** **Ashby**


**Starting Price** Free (ATS); $199/month for premium features including AI scoring ~$400/month (Foundations plan, up to 100 employees)


**Free Tier** Yes, with unlimited jobs, users, and candidates No


**Setup Time** Minutes, no training needed Days of training or a month of light use


**Job Board Distribution** 100+ boards, one-click posting Standard job board integrations


**AI Capabilities** Built-in resume scoring (0-100), AI job descriptions, career pages Machine learning scoring; requires configuration before results improve


**Sourcing Tools** Chrome extension with two-click outreach and pre-written templates Chrome extension with multi-channel campaigns; complex setup required


**Analytics** Startup-focused dashboard: time-to-hire, pipeline drop-off, cost-per-hire Business intelligence-level reporting; sold as a standalone product


**Recruiter Access** On-demand fractional recruiters averaging $75-125/hr; typically $2,000-7,000 per hire (rates vary) Software only; no recruiter marketplace


**Best For** Startups and founders filling 1-10 roles who need speed and cost control Scaling companies with experienced recruiting teams managing 5+ roles simultaneously


## What Is Ashby?


Ashby is an all-in-one[recruiting system](https://www.dover.com/blog/the-game-theory-of-recruiting) that combines applicant tracking, sourcing, scheduling automation, and analytics into a single interface. The software is built for companies with experienced recruiting teams who want to consolidate their hiring tech stack.


The typical Ashby customer is a scaling company managing multiple open roles simultaneously, usually 5 or more positions at a time. These teams are often making dozens of hires per year and need features to handle high application volumes and coordinate complex interview processes across departments.


Ashby takes a data-driven approach to hiring. The system provides deep analytics and reporting capabilities that let recruiting teams track conversion rates, pipeline health, and hiring velocity. It also includes built-in sourcing tools and scheduling automation designed to reduce manual work for coordinators and recruiters who are filling many roles at once.


## What is Dover?


Dover is an all-in-one recruiting solution built for startups and early-stage companies. The product combines a free applicant tracking system with on-demand access to fractional recruiters, letting you handle hiring with software, services, or both.


Most Dover customers are founders or small teams at startups filling one to ten roles who need to scale hiring quickly without building an entire in-house recruiting function.


The core differentiator is flexibility. You can use the ATS for free to manage your hiring process, then tap into a marketplace of[vetted recruiters on an hourly basis](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-guide) when you need extra help with sourcing or coordination. This fractional model means you pay only for the recruiting support you actually use, avoiding the hefty placement fees that traditional agencies charge.


Where the model matters most is at the inflection point between self-serve hiring and needing more capacity. For roles with strong inbound volume and clear requirements, the ATS can typically handle the full process on its own. When a role is senior, specialized, or requires sourcing passive candidates, or when the team simply lacks recruiting bandwidth, a fractional recruiter can step in without switching systems. Because the recruiter works inside the same pipeline the hiring team sees, there is no coordination overhead, no duplicate outreach, and no visibility gaps in the candidate flow.


## ATS and Core Recruiting Features


Both systems offer full[applicant tracking capabilities](https://www.dover.com/blog/best-applicant-tracking-systems-startups-top-6) , but they differ in complexity and setup time.


### Ashby’s Interface Complexity


Ashby features a complex user interface with a steep learning curve that requires more clicks than average ATS systems. The Interview and Scheduling section has a lot of settings tabs, and common tasks like creating job openings require more clicks than most competitors.


Their Help Centre acknowledges teams need a few days of training or a month of light use to get comfortable. The careers page functionality is limited and not suitable for creating professional company career sites.


### Dover’s Easy Setup


Dover’s ATS is ready to use in minutes with no training required. The interface is built for quick adoption, so you can start posting jobs and reviewing candidates immediately without going through complex settings.


Dover includes AI-generated career pages and job descriptions that create professional company branding automatically. One-click job board distribution posts your openings to 100+ boards simultaneously, with all applicants flowing into a centralized pipeline. AI-powered resume scoring (available on the $199/month premium plan) ranks candidates and surfaces top talent without manual sorting.


## Sourcing and Candidate Outreach


### Ashby’s Multi-Channel Approach


Ashby offers AI email personalization for outreach campaigns, automated subject line testing, and multi-channel coordination across email, LinkedIn, and SMS. A Chrome extension handles sourcing while CRM capabilities manage talent pools.


The sourcing functionality requires learning complex workflows and configuration settings. Teams spend time understanding proper campaign and sequence setup before seeing results.


### Dover’s Simplified Sourcing


Dover’s Chrome extension finds candidate email addresses and allows for personalized outreach in two clicks. The tool integrates with the ATS, letting you add candidates to active pipelines without switching systems.


Pre-written email templates optimized for startup recruiting come with automated follow-up sequences built in. You can start sourcing passive candidates immediately without training on multi-step processes or crafting outreach messaging from scratch.


## Pricing and Cost Structure


Ashby uses a three-tier, company-size pricing model. The Foundations plan starts at roughly $400/month and covers companies with up to 100 employees, based on approximately $5 to $8 per employee per month. The Plus plan serves companies with 101 to 1,000 employees and requires contacting Ashby for custom pricing. Enterprise, for organizations above 1,000 employees, also requires direct negotiation. Both Plus and Enterprise pricing vary by company size, usage, and commitment level.


This structure means your ATS cost scales alongside headcount. A 50-person company can expect to spend several hundred dollars monthly, while a 200-person organization moves into custom pricing territory, with no published ceiling. Some users also report that add-ons and advanced analytics features are not included in base plans, which can push the total cost higher depending on the package.


Dover’s ATS is free with unlimited jobs, users, and candidates. There are no monthly fees, per-seat charges, or hidden costs for the recruiting software.


The only cost comes from engaging fractional recruiters through Dover’s marketplace, with rates averaging $75-$125/hour (actual rates can be higher or lower). Companies typically spend $2,000-$7,000 per hire using fractional recruiters versus $30,000+ for traditional contingency recruiting, though costs vary by role and scope. You can also use the free ATS indefinitely without spending anything.


## AI and Automation Capabilities


### Ashby’s AI Features


Ashby uses[machine learning algorithms](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/machine-learning-algorithms/) to analyze and score candidates based on job requirements and company culture fit. AI assistance appears throughout the product, automating routine tasks like application review and providing insights to recruiting teams.


The challenge is implementation. These advanced AI features require a lot of configuration to work effectively within Ashby’s complex workflows. Teams need to spend time training the algorithms and setting up scoring criteria before seeing accurate results.


### Dover’s Plug-and-Play AI


Dover built AI directly into core recruiting workflows so it works immediately without configuration.[Resume scoring](https://www.dover.com/blog/ai-recruiting-software-ats) analyzes every applicant automatically, ranking candidates by fit and surfacing top talent first. The AI also generates complete job descriptions and professional career pages in seconds.


Intelligent candidate matching runs in the background, identifying the most qualified applicants for each role without manual input. You get AI-powered recruiting from day one, no setup required.


## Analytics and Reporting


### Ashby’s Advanced Analytics


Ashby delivers business intelligence-level reporting with analytics so detailed the company sells them as a standalone product. The system includes extensive dashboards and data visualization tools that rival dedicated reporting systems.


The tradeoff is complexity. Setting up and interpreting these reports requires going through extensive configuration options and understanding multiple data visualization formats, which adds time before you can extract useful insights.


### Dover’s Startup-Focused Metrics


Dover provides real-time analytics built for quick decisions. The dashboard surfaces important metrics like time-to-hire, pipeline drop-off rates, and offer acceptance rates with straightforward visualizations that require no configuration.


The system includes full recruiting cost transparency, displaying exact cost-per-hire data when you work with fractional recruiters. This lets you track ROI and compare recruiting performance across roles without exporting data or building custom reports.


## Why Dover is the Better Choice


Startups filling their first roles face different challenges than companies managing dozens of simultaneous hires. Dover was built for this reality, where speed matters more than configuring advanced analytics workflows.


For roles with steady inbound volume and clear requirements, the ATS can handle the full process on its own. Job distribution, applicant tracking, and interview scheduling work without recruiter involvement, and most early-stage companies can fill straightforward roles this way at zero software cost. Teams that want AI resume scoring can add the premium plan at $199/month.[Over 98% of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.jobscan.co/blog/fortune-500-use-applicant-tracking-systems/) now use applicant tracking systems, but cost structure matters more than enterprise-feature parity for most startups filling their first ten roles.


The calculus changes when roles are senior, specialized, or require sourcing candidates who aren’t actively applying. A fractional[recruiting model](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-dover-s-recruiting-model-builds-in-accountability-from-day-one) plugs into the ATS at that inflection point without adding a new system. A vetted startup recruiter steps in on top of the existing pipeline, works from the same candidate data the internal team sees, and steps back when the role is filled. Because both parties share one pipeline, there’s no coordination lag and no blind spots in the candidate flow.


[The applicant tracking market continues growing](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/applicant-tracking-system-market-109826) as more companies recognize the cost of managing hiring without infrastructure. Ashby’s[2026 Talent Trends Report](https://www.ashbyhq.com/talent-trends-report/reports/startup-hiring) found that over half of startup talent teams are now using AI across multiple hiring workflows, and startups that bring in recruiters earlier cut time-to-hire by nearly a third. The question for most startups isn’t whether to use an ATS. It’s whether that system can also scale recruiting capacity when searches require more than software alone. A simple pipeline tool works well for early, inbound-heavy roles; when hiring gets harder, having fractional recruiting capacity inside the same system avoids the overhead of coordinating with a separate vendor. That’s the point where tool selection and recruiting strategy intersect.


## FAQs


### Can I start using Dover immediately without training?


Yes, Dover’s ATS is ready to use in minutes with no training required. You can sign up, invite your team, and start posting jobs right away, with AI automatically generating job descriptions and career pages for you.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


For many early-stage roles with solid inbound volume, the ATS can handle the full process on its own. The decision to add a recruiter comes down to role complexity and bandwidth. Sourcing passive candidates, filling senior or specialized roles, and managing high application volumes without internal recruiting capacity are the points where software alone may not be enough. When you do bring in a fractional recruiter, the shared pipeline means no handoff lag and no visibility gaps. The ATS builds the foundation; fractional recruiting adds capacity on top when the search calls for more.


### When should I consider using fractional recruiters instead of doing it myself?


Consider[fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-fractional-recruiter-when-startup-needs-one) when you need help with sourcing passive candidates, screening high application volumes, or coordinating complex interview processes but don’t want to hire a full-time recruiter or pay agency placement fees. You can scale recruiting support up or down based on your current hiring needs.


## Final Thoughts on Selecting the Right Recruiting Software


The ATS comparison between Dover and Ashby reveals two different philosophies about[recruiting software](https://www.dover.com/) . Dover built a free system that works immediately, with optional access to vetted recruiters when you need extra bandwidth. Ashby offers deep analytics and complex workflows that require training and scale with headcount. For startups needing speed and cost control, Dover removes the barriers between you and your next great hire.
